title: Styles and computed styles
learningObjectives: Explain styles and computed styles and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: The Styles panel shows matched CSS rules and declarations, including overridden rules. The Computed panel shows resolved property values after the cascade and value computation. Developer tools can also show inherited rules, source locations, and box-model dimensions.
understand.whyItMatters: These panels help trace why a style is or is not applied. Inspect the winning declaration before adding another override.
understand.analogy: Styles shows the competing instructions; Computed shows the final result after the browser resolves them.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: getComputedStyle reads resolved style values for an element. Developer tools provide a richer view of the source declarations and cascade.

examples.explanation: getComputedStyle reads resolved style values for an element. Developer tools provide a richer view of the source declarations and cascade.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Create a specificity conflict and use Styles and Computed to identify which declaration wins and why.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
